intended_use: Preregistered public development corpus for the Codex-only three-arm comparison. It asks again whether the full reviewer workflow beats the pattern catalog alone, on cases written after the severity-exception wording was added to the skill, and whether documented severity exceptions are applied on cases no model has seen. It is not sealed and does not establish generalization.
contamination_risk: The corpus is inspectable and was written by the same author who wrote the reviewer references it exercises. It was designed from the reference contracts alone, without reading any v9 run report. Every result must disclose that exposure and remain development evidence.

labeling.procedure: Single-author labels written from the reviewer references at the frozen skill commit, before any model call on this corpus, and without reading any earlier holdout run report. Every label records the reference rule that decides it, quoting or citing the contract text, and every case records which prompt arm is expected to get it right and why. Blind double labeling is pending. After authoring, a Claude subagent and Codex gpt-5.6-sol each labeled all 30 cases blind from copies of the case sources and the skill, without the corpus file. 100 of the 103 finding and guard labels matched both. An arbiter subagent resolved 4 disputes from quoted contract text, and the user approved the result on 2026-09-26.
labeling.limitations: Labels were authored by one agent, then checked by two blind labelers and an arbiter; all are models, not human experts. No model has been run on the corpus. Optional labels mark contract boundaries where the references support two readings, including a second pattern for the same gap and a contested severity. Code is synthetic and original.
labeling.instance_severities: Labels may use an instance severity that the references define but the Quick Reference does not list: #1 at P1 when one promised outcome is verified and another is not, #23 at P0 when a guard-suppressed render lets an empty-state or negative assertion pass, #2 at P1 when one promised effect is verified and another is not (reporting.md P0 boundary), and, as optional labels only, #4k at P0 when an assertion loop over an unproven collection is the test's only verification (reporting.md: an instance can be reported higher when it meets the P0 definition outright).

The branch holds only an action and the stop title is asserted unconditionally afterwards. pattern-reference.md #5a: "conditionally dismissing an optional blocker before an unconditional promised-outcome assertion is an action-only branch, not this bypass"; semantic-review.md 5a: "SKIP action-only branches."

pattern-reference.md #5a: "Flag P0 only when the conditional assertion is load-bearing for the title/action's promised outcome and the false branch has no independent unconditional meaningful postcondition". The offline pack is the promised outcome and nothing checks it when the element is absent.

The withdraw test proves the request the app sent but never checks the promised list removal (#2 P1); the visit test verifies nothing (#2 P0).
